past_recommendations.text: Reversal first-flag counter unchanged at 81; three first-flags since 07-01. Regime-explained, no finding.

Close the #11 days_to_1atr boundary item — the two blank-days_to_1atr/mfe=1.00 rows (MU@2026-05-27 reversal, MXL@2026-07-21 bounce) are the documented pre-07-31 2-decimal display artifact, not a comparison bug; stop carrying it as QA.

Retire the reversal `pct_from_9ema ≤ 0.10` floor as an adoption candidate — it is a cap-mix confound (14/19 in-cell rows are Large-cap; within-cap gaps are 8pp cw on 11 clusters and n=4). Stop carrying it forward and add it to the settled-questions record alongside the score-tier inversion.
Open a Medium-cap-only watch on reversal `pct_from_9ema` in the opposite direction — Medium ≤0.20 cw 46% (14 cl) vs >0.20 cw 76% (14 cl); revisit once either cell reaches 20 clusters.

Promote reversal `prior_day_rvol ≥ 1.5` to primary candidate inside the ~100-first-flag RVOL-tier restructure; require ≥20 clusters *within Large and within Medium separately* before any re-key, since the pooled result is cap-confounded (counter: 81 reversal first-flags).
Keep bounce `pct_change_3` → −0.15 staged; execute on the next non-wave bounce first-flag landing in the >−0.15 cell (needs exactly 1 more cluster).

Report bounce rates cluster-weighted by default in the next cycle — `bounce_2026-07-28` and `bounce_2026-07-17` supply 35% of first-flags and 44% of winners, and the pooled figure overstates the bucket by 9.3pp.
Re-affirm the 1.5-ATR stop with this cycle's earliness numbers (36/38 reversal winners and 73/73 bounce winners survive it); no confirmation-trigger or entry-delay work is warranted.

No first-flags added since #15 — before the next analysis, confirm whether the pipeline is producing signals at all or only reprints, since three consecutive staged items are now blocked purely on sample arrival.

reversal | Large | GO eligibility (all score tiers) | GO at score >= 4/5 | suspend Large-cap reversal GO; route to CAUTION/no-trade pending a Large-specific discriminator | Large 12/37 pooled, cw 27.2% over 23 clusters vs Medium 25/38, cw 64.4% over 22 clusters — both cells clear the 20-cluster gate; within Large the scorer is flat (5/5 5/15 cw 26.9%/13cl, 4/5 5/14 cw 34.4%/8cl, 3/5 2/8 cw 26.7%/5cl), so no score-tier restructure recovers it
Execute the Large-cap reversal suspension above; it is the only change this cycle clearing both the 20-cluster gate and cap-stratification.

Kill the staged bounce pct_change_3 → −0.15 item and move it to the settled-questions record as "knife-edge at −0.15, no separation at −0.12/−0.17/−0.20; cap-mix driven" — do not re-stage it on a row-count trigger.

Add a neighborhood-sweep requirement to the guardrails — before adopting any threshold, report the pass/fail cluster-weighted rates at the candidate cut and at two nearby cuts on each side; reject cuts whose separation does not degrade monotonically.
Hold #15's promotion of reversal persistence to a scored input for one more cycle — the prior-print-tradeable cell fell from 20 to 19 clusters as new episodes chained; re-check at the next analysis.
Downgrade the #16 Medium-cap reversal pct_from_9ema watch from 30pp to 11pp (cw 69.0%/14cl vs 57.7%/13cl); keep it open but stop treating it as a promotion candidate.
Keep accumulating bounce Large toward 20 clusters before touching Large GapFade thresholds — now 10 clusters (18/21, cw 85.0%), up from 6 at #15.

Track the reversal gap_pct inversion toward its own adoption test — the negative-gap cell is now 15 clusters (cw 64.4% vs 37.4%); at 20 clusters it becomes the strongest demotion candidate in the reversal criteria set, ahead of the RVOL re-key.

Re-affirm the 1.5-ATR stop in the playbook with this cycle's numbers (35/37 reversal and 41/41 bounce first-flag winners survive it) and close the confirmation-trigger question again — D0 confirmation forfeits 34% of reversal and 46% of bounce winners.

reversal | Large | GO eligibility (all score tiers) | GO at score >= 4/5 | suspend Large-cap reversal GO; route to CAUTION/no-trade | re-confirmed and strengthened vs #17: Large 11/33 pooled, cw 25.8% over 21 clusters vs Medium 24/35, cw 64.3% over 21 clusters — both clear the 20-cluster gate; flat within Large across score tiers (5/5 cw 25.0%/14 cl, 4/5 cw 32.5%/10 cl); no discriminator rescues it (rvol>=1.5 cw 38.5%/13 cl, gap<0 cw 42.9%/7 cl, pct_change_3>=0.20 cw 44.4%/9 cl); August cohort 2/6 confirms out-of-sample
Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension from #17 — it was not shipped, six Large reversal GOs fired in August and went 2/6, and the evidence is now stronger (21 clusters per side).

Retire the reversal `prior_day_rvol >= 1.5` promotion from #16 and move it to the settled-questions record as "Large-only, and inverted within Medium (cw 60.4% vs 68.2%); the pooled result was a cap confound."

Downgrade the reversal `gap_pct` inversion from #17's "strongest demotion candidate" to a Large-cap restatement — Medium is +4.2pp, the negative-gap cell fell from 15 to 14 clusters, and suspending Large removes the effect entirely. Stop tracking it toward a 20-cluster adoption test.
Close the #16/#17 Medium-cap reversal `pct_from_9ema` watch — separation is now −1.5pp at 0.20 and flips sign at 0.22.

Kill bounce persistence as a scored-input candidate and record it as an overlap artifact — at target-date lag ≥2 days the effect is −1.9pp (76.7% vs 78.6%); the pooled +26.7pp comes entirely from 1-day-lag reprints whose windows overlap the prior print's.

Hold reversal persistence one more cycle with a specific trigger — it survives the overlap control in both lag strata (+28.5pp at 1-day, +59.7pp at ≥2-day) but the clean ≥2-day-lag stratum is only 7 clusters; promote to a scored input when that stratum reaches 20 clusters, not when the pooled cell does.

Open a bounce watch on the "sharp flush, intact chart" pair — `selloff_total_pct <= -0.25` (cw 90.5%, 14 cl) combined with `pct_off_52wk_high >= -0.35` (cw 83.3%, 14 cl); both sweeps are monotonic and the second runs against the current criterion direction. Revisit at 20 clusters per cell.

Fix the earliness instrumentation for bounces — `adverse_before_fav_atr` and `days_to_1atr` are emitted only on the 1-ATR hit, so 36 of 75 bounce first-flag winners have no stop/earliness data; emit an `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the actual per-bucket gate so stop-placement claims cover the full winner set.
Keep accumulating bounce Large toward 20 clusters — unchanged at 10 clusters (18/21, cw 85.0%) since #17, i.e. no new Large bounce first-flags this cycle; do not touch Large GapFade thresholds.
Report the reversal first-flag counter as recovered — 14 August first-flags after 1 in July; the #17 note about three staged items blocked on sample arrival no longer applies to the reversal bucket.

reversal | Large | GO eligibility (all score tiers) | GO at score >= 4/5 | suspend Large-cap reversal GO; route to CAUTION/no-trade | third consecutive confirmation — visible-window Large 11/29 = 37.9% vs Medium 21/30 = 70.0%; #18 measured 11/33 cw 25.8% over 21 clusters vs Medium 24/35 cw 64.3% over 21 clusters, both past the 20-cluster gate; flat within Large across score tiers at #18 (5/5 cw 25.0%/14 cl, 4/5 cw 32.5%/10 cl) and no discriminator rescues it; October added only 1 Large first-flag (SPCX 10-06, tradeable), which does not move a 21-cluster estimate

Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension — it has now been recommended at #17, #18 and #19 and remains unshipped; every cycle it stays live costs Large-cap reversal GOs at roughly half the Medium hit rate.

Correct the CLUSTER DAY rationale — the 7-14 breadth band has flipped sign from -0.50R/10 sessions (the figure quoted in the priority_report comment justifying the 7→15 raise) to +0.40R/11 sessions; update the comment to the current numbers and note that the band is single-session-sensitive.
Withhold CLUSTER DAY threshold recalibration — the 15+ band is at 3 sessions against a 20-session requirement; re-check when it reaches 20, not on row count (it already has 254 rows).

Split the #18 bounce depth pair — keep `selloff_total_pct <= -0.25` as an open watch (14 clusters, cw 97.6%, monotonic sweep: -0.22 → 75.0%, -0.25 → 95.8%, -0.28 → 92.3%) and retire the `pct_off_52wk_high >= -0.35` leg to the settled-questions record as "decayed to +6.7 pp pooled / 79.2% cw over 16 clusters once 2026-10-16 landed; not a candidate."

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix from #18 — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the actual per-bucket gate; it is still unshipped and October bounce winners (BE, CRWV 2026-10-15) still have no usable stop-placement data, which is why earliness analysis remains reversal-only.
Hold reversal persistence for another cycle — the clean ≥2-day-lag stratum moved 7 → 8 clusters against a 20-cluster promotion trigger; do not promote on the pooled cell.
Keep accumulating bounce Large — zero new Large bounce first-flags this cycle, still ~10 clusters; Large GapFade thresholds stay frozen.

Record that the bounce scorer carries no information below the bar — cluster-weighted tradeable_3d is flat across scores 0-3 (53.3 / 59.8 / 53.8 / 55.4) and so is median entry_r (1.52 / 1.63 / 1.52 / 1.49); treat score 4+ as a binary gate plus quantity limiter and stop reporting below-bar score tiers as a curve.

reversal | Large | GO eligibility (all score tiers) | GO at score >= 4/5 | suspend Large-cap reversal GO; route to CAUTION/no-trade | fourth consecutive confirmation — visible-window Large 11/28 = 39.3%, cw 33.8% over 18 clusters vs Medium 21/30 = 70.0%, cw 64.9% over 19 clusters; #18 measured cw 25.8%/21 cl vs 64.3%/21 cl on the full log, both past the 20-cluster gate; flat within Large by tier (5/5 cw 33.3%/12 cl, 4/5 cw 40.6%/8 cl) and no criterion rescues it; October added one Large first-flag (SPCX 10-06, tradeable), which cannot move a 21-cluster estimate

bounce | POOLED | gap_pct | scored criterion, 1 of 6, cap-keyed (-0.03 Medium/_default, -0.08 Large, -0.04 ETF, -0.09 Small/Micro) | promote to a weighted/required criterion at <= -0.03 pooled — a bounce that fails it should not reach score 4 on the other five alone | pass 51/59 = 86.4%, cw 73.8% (21 clusters) vs fail 15/30 = 50.0%, cw 58.7% (23 clusters); both cells past the 20-cluster gate; holds at cw 72.5% (20 cl) vs 58.7% (23 cl) after removing the largest cluster. Caveat stated plainly: a hard veto here would drop 30 signals of which 15 were winners, so implement as weighting, not as a veto

bounce | POOLED | pct_change_3 | scored criterion, cap-keyed p75-of-winners (-0.14 to -0.30) | promote to a weighted/required criterion at <= -0.15 pooled | pass 57/71 = 80.3%, cw 73.0% (28 clusters) vs fail 26/41 = 63.4%, cw 57.1% (26 clusters); the most cluster-robust cut in the data — still +15.0 pp with 24 clusters per side after removing the four largest clusters. Same caveat: as a hard veto it discards 26 winners to avoid 15 losers, so weight it rather than gate on it
Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension — recommended at #17, #18, #19 and now #20, still unshipped; four cycles of Large running at roughly half Medium's hit rate.

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix from #18/#19 — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the per-bucket gate; still unshipped, and October bounce winners again have no stop-placement data, which is why earliness analysis remains reversal-only for a third cycle.

Update the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — the 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions now reads +0.10R/12 sessions, and has read −0.50 → +0.40 → +0.10 across three cycles; record it as single-session-sensitive and unsuitable as a justification.
Add a thin-day damp on the 0–2 breadth band — 25 sessions, EV −0.33R, win 34.5%; this is the only breadth band with ≥20 sessions and the EV gradient across bands is monotonic.

Prioritise and size bounce entries by score tier rather than treating 4/6 and 5/6 as equivalent — GO median entry_r 2.56R / 79% ≥1R vs CAUTION 1.55R / 66%, cluster-weighted 3.25R over 20 GO clusters vs 1.70R over 50 CAUTION clusters, robust to removing 2026-10-15. This does not reopen the settled GO-vs-CAUTION `tradeable_3d` comparison; it is a magnitude finding on a different metric. When quantity must be capped on a broad day, drop CAUTION first.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables — the supplied magnitude table is row-pooled, and entry_r is heavily right-skewed (top rows run 9R–17R), so row medians cannot be audited for cluster concentration without re-deriving them.

Open a bounce watch on the joint "fails both `gap_pct <= -0.03` and `pct_change_3 <= -0.15`" veto — 3/12 tradeable, cw 30.0% over 10 clusters, the cleanest loser-selector in the data; promote to a hard veto when that cell reaches 20 clusters, not before.
Keep `selloff_total_pct <= -0.25` as an open bounce watch — 15 clusters (was 14), cw 93.3%, sweep still monotonic through −0.25; revisit at 20 clusters.

Hold reversal persistence another cycle — the overlap-clean lag ≥2 stratum is 4 clusters in the visible window (8 on the full log), against a 20-cluster promotion trigger. Do not promote on the pooled cell.

Record `premarket_rvol` as a session confound, not a reversal feature — all 18 evening reversal first-flags carry a nonzero value against 8 of 42 morning ones, and the apparent +16.9 pp edge is the morning/evening split (cw 59%/13 cl vs 43%/23 cl).
Keep accumulating bounce Large — 11 clusters (19/22, cw 86.4%), up one from #19 but still under the gate; GapFade Large thresholds stay frozen.

Execute the Large-cap reversal GO suspension — now recommended at #17, #18, #19, #20 and #21 and still unshipped; Large runs cw 35.8% over 17 clusters against Medium's 64.9% over 19, five cycles running.

Ship the earliness instrumentation fix — emit `adverse_before_gate_atr` and `days_to_gate` keyed to the actual per-bucket gate; unshipped since #18, and earliness analysis is now reversal-only for a fourth consecutive cycle.

Emit cluster-weighted `entry_r` by score tier in the pre-aggregated tables (requested at #20, still row-pooled); entry_r is heavily right-skewed, so the by-score medians now driving the entry-bar verdict cannot be audited for cluster concentration.

Open a watch on moving the bounce entry bar from score 4 to score 5 — median entry_r is flat 1.54–1.80R across scores 0–4 and jumps to 2.50R only at 5; settle it when score 6 reaches 20 clusters (currently 4) so the top of the curve can be read as a trend rather than one spiking tier.

Update the priority_report CLUSTER DAY comment — the 7–14 band it cites as −0.50R/10 sessions now reads +0.10R/12 sessions, a sign flip and the third different value in three cycles; mark it single-session-sensitive and unusable as justification.
Add the thin-day damp on the 0–2 breadth band (25 sessions, EV −0.33R, win 34.5%) — the only breadth band with ≥20 sessions, and the EV gradient across bands is monotonic.

Carry a new reversal watch that `prior_day_rvol >= 2.0` separates backwards (pass cw 42.9%/14 cl vs fail cw 52.2%/24 cl, widening to −25.4 pp at 2.5); do not act until the passing cell reaches 20 clusters.

Record that Analysis #21 added zero new first-flags in either bucket — all criterion cells reproduce #20 exactly — and consider spacing the next analysis to signal arrival rather than to a fixed cadence, since re-running on an unchanged sample produces no new information.
